item.research_question: How to design and develop ultralight-weight complex concentrated alloys (ULW-CCAs) with high strength, low modulus, and good ductility?
item.processing_route: Induction melting in an argon atmosphere and a graphite crucible, followed by casting into a copper mold
item.test_conditions: Compression tests at a strain rate of 1 × 10−4 s−1, nanoindentation tests with a maximum load of 8 mN
key_findings: The Al19.9Li30Mg35Si10Ca5Y0.1 ULW-CCA exhibits a high fracture strength of 710 ± 26 MPa and yield strength of 556 ± 20 MPa
The Al15Li35Mg48Ca1Si1 ULW-CCA shows a good combination of mechanical properties, including a relatively high yield strength of 342 ± 19 MPa and a high compressive ductility of >45%
The Al15Li39Mg45Ca0.5Si0.5 ULW-CCA displays a good ductility of >60% and a low density of 1.46 ± 0.05 g cm−3
The volume fraction of solid solution phases plays a significant role in the plastic deformation of the ULW-CCAs
The low Young’s modulus of the ULW-CCAs is mainly dominated by the large volume fraction of solid solution phases
item.mechanism: The solid solution phases play a significant role in the plastic deformation of the ULW-CCAs, and the low Young’s modulus is mainly dominated by the large volume fraction of solid solution phases
item.limitations: The ULW-CCAs usually have some major drawbacks, such as a brittle nature and hard processability due to big differences between melting and boiling temperatures from different constitute elements
item.future_work: Further research is needed to explore the potential applications of the ULW-CCAs in the field of light-weight structure materials
quotes: the development of ultralight-weight complex concentrated alloys (ULW-CCAs) to approach a high specific strength is important for the structural material field

records.text: Paper card. Question: How to design and develop ultralight-weight complex concentrated alloys (ULW-CCAs) with high strength, low modulus, and good ductility?. System: Al-Li-Mg-Ca-Si-Y complex concentrated alloys. Processing: Induction melting in an argon atmosphere and a graphite crucible, followed by casting into a copper mold. Test conditions: Compression tests at a strain rate of 1 × 10−4 s−1, nanoindentation tests with a maximum load of 8 mN. Findings: The Al19.9Li30Mg35Si10Ca5Y0.1 ULW-CCA exhibits a high fracture strength of 710 ± 26 MPa and yield strength of 556 ± 20 MPa; The Al15Li35Mg48Ca1Si1 ULW-CCA shows a good combination of mechanical properties, including a relatively high yield strength of 342 ± 19 MPa and a high compressive ductility of >45%; The Al15Li39Mg45Ca0.5Si0.5 ULW-CCA displays a good ductility of >60% and a low density of 1.46 ± 0.05 g cm−3; The volume fraction of solid solution phases plays a significant role in the plastic deformation of the ULW-CCAs; The low Young’s modulus of the ULW-CCAs is mainly dominated by the large volume fraction of solid solution phases. Mechanism: The solid solution phases play a significant role in the plastic deformation of the ULW-CCAs, and the low Young’s modulus is mainly dominated by the large volume fraction of solid solution phases. Limitations: The ULW-CCAs usually have some major drawbacks, such as a brittle nature and hard processability due to big differences between melting and boiling temperatures from different constitute elements. Future work: Further research is needed to explore the potential applications of the ULW-CCAs in the field of light-weight structure materials. Quote: "the development of ultralight-weight complex concentrated alloys (ULW-CCAs) to approach a high specific strength is important for the structural material field"
